data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Safety-critical systems are designed under unified governance, so diversity can be mandated; decentralized networks rely on spontaneous or market-driven diversity.","Safety-critical systems prioritize zero failures; decentralized networks often tolerate higher baseline failure rates."],"overturn_conditions":["It is demonstrated that small services can maintain both architectural diversity and internal redundancy without trade-offs.","Evidence shows that decentralized networks without mandated diversity still avoid correlated failures."],"shared_structure":["A network of independent components designed to prevent common-mode failure.","Diversity as the primary defense against correlated triggers."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["Without enforced diversity, decentralized networks are vulnerable to the same common-mode failures as monolithic systems.","If diversity is present, the network trades correlated failure risk for higher uncorrelated failure risk."]},"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure solely if it exhibits validated architectural diversity, but this resilience is purchased at the cost of high baseline failure rates from uncorrelated causes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The small services are homogeneous in architecture, meaning a single bug affects them all simultaneously.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service successfully implements internal architectural diversity rather than mere component replication.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralization succeeds in resisting correlated failure only when the independent services are architecturally heterogeneous (different languages, libraries, infrastructure). This heterogeneity ensures that a single bug or vulnerability cannot propagate across the entire network. However, smaller services lack the resources to implement the comprehensive internal redundancy and exhaustive testing of a large service. Consequently, while the decentralized network eliminates the single point of failure (correlated risk), it dramatically increases the constant rate of independent node failures (uncorrelated risk).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
